brief:
The Guardian reported this week that Britain's foreign policy is adopting an "ethical dimension" under the current government, reviving an approach last seen nearly three decades ago when Labour's Robin Cook took office as Foreign Secretary. The move represents a deliberate shift away from purely strategic calculations, even amid the Trump era's geopolitical pressures.

The government is centering human rights and moral considerations in diplomatic decisions, following Cook's model from the 1990s. Labour is positioning Britain's international approach differently from its predecessor's posture, with foreign policy choices reflecting values-based commitments alongside strategic interests.

title: Britain signals return to ethics-focused foreign policy under Labour
